name: European compound summer
headline: Persistent alternating highs and lows (WMO).
numbers: France, excess deaths: at least 1,000 additional deaths in the first three days (Public Health France, as reported on 28 June). France, heat-related deaths estimated by attribution: more than 2,700 (Carbon Brief analysis). France, excess deaths from 17 June to 2 July: 5,764, 36.2 percent above normal (a later report). The three figures use different methods and are not added together.

sections.The setup: Dry April–June, successive heatwaves; hottest June on record for western Europe (Copernicus); July the second hottest (22.48 °C, +2.53 °C, just below July 2006; Copernicus) and the hottest July on record for France (+3.8 °C; Météo-France).
sections.What amplified it: Dry soils intensified heat; in July 2026 large wildfires burned in southwestern France (Gironde) and in Spain (Avila and Madrid provinces; WWA and Imperial College: central and eastern Spain), NASA Earth Observatory, 31 July 2026; in June 2026 sea surface temperatures in parts of the Mediterranean were up to 6 °C above normal (WWA, citing a European Union source).
sections.Climate signal: WWA attributes about 2 °C of the heating of the studied Mediterranean marine heatwaves to human-induced climate change (WWA, 19 August 2026); marine heat virtually impossible pre-industrial (WWA).
sections.Still open: Summary entry: the full deep-dive (day-by-day timeline, steering, how it ended, sources) has not been written yet. It will be added as the log works back through the year.
